title: Nasdaq Drops 2.1% for the Week as AI Spending Fears Hammer Memory Chip Stocks
excerpt: Alphabet's capital spending surge spooked investors ahead of megacap earnings, while falling oil prices offered Wall Street partial relief.
body:
• The Nasdaq Composite fell 0.6% on Friday and lost 2.1% for the week — its worst weekly performance among major indexes.
  • Memory chip stocks led the decline: Sandisk plunged over 10%, while Western Digital and Seagate each dropped more than 7%.
  • Alphabet's announcement of higher capital spending on AI infrastructure, even as cash flow turned negative, triggered a broader re-evaluation of big tech valuations.
  • Falling oil prices and hopes for US-Iran diplomacy provided partial support, with Brent crude dipping below $100 and the Dow adding 0.5%.

A Week the Bulls Would Rather Forget

Wall Street ended the week on a fractured note Friday. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 235 points, or 0.5%, to close at 51,947. The S&P 500 eked out a 0.07% gain. But the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite fell 157 points, or 0.6%, to 24,980 — capping a 2.1% weekly loss that made it the worst-performing major index.

The divergence reflected a market split between old-economy stocks benefiting from lower energy costs and technology names weighed down by concerns about the sustainability of artificial intelligence spending.

Memory Chips Take the Hardest Hit

Sandisk was the worst performer in the S&P 500 on Friday, falling more than 10% and breaking below its 50-day moving average. Western Digital and Seagate Technology each dropped more than 7%. Micron Technology undercut a key technical support level.

The sell-off in memory stocks has been building for weeks. Sandisk and Micron have shed 39% and 27% respectively from record highs hit last month, though both remain up triple digits for the year. Morgan Stanley earlier this week called the pullback a "strong entry point," noting that multi-year purchasing agreements would stabilize the cycle even if they capped peak earnings.

Alphabet's Cash Burn Rattled Confidence

The catalyst for the broader tech retreat was Alphabet's second-quarter earnings report late Wednesday, in which the company announced plans to accelerate capital expenditure on AI infrastructure — even as its cash flow turned negative for the quarter. The market's reaction rippled through chip stocks and AI-adjacent names.

"The fear of missing out is becoming more like a fear of massive overbuilding."

— Peter Andersen, CEO, Andersen Capital Management

Intel reported stronger-than-expected quarterly results Thursday night — revenue of $16.1 billion, up 25% year over year — but its shares still fell Friday, dragged down by the sector-wide sentiment.

Oil and Geopolitics

Some relief came from falling energy prices. West Texas Intermediate crude dropped more than 2% to around $90.10 per barrel, while Brent crude slipped below $100 to roughly $98. A Reuters report that Pakistan is working to restart stalled talks between the US and Iran provided a brief afternoon lift before tech selling overwhelmed the rally.

The 10-year Treasury yield fell 2 basis points to 4.68%. Bitcoin traded around $64,200, down modestly.
nri_angle: Indian-origin tech workers and NRI investors with heavy exposure to AI and chip stocks are directly affected by the valuation re-rating.
